newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian newspaper rejects demands for apology.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian newspaper rejects demands for apology.

text.p: Indonesia's top English language newspaper on Friday rejected a demand by the country's state-owned aircraft manufacturer to apologise in foreign media for a report about a crash involving one of its planes.
The Jakarta Post issued an apology following an erroneous front-page report on May 23 about a crash the day before involving a military plane built by Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN).

Indonesian authorities, however, said a faulty parachute cord had triggered the crash during a low-altitude test flight. The IPTN is controlled by high-profile Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie.
The newspaper printed a retraction and an apology on May 24.
Lubis said the paper took necessary action quickly after the report was printed and that the press law did not say apologies should also be printed in foreign media.

"The demand is exaggerated. We have to reject it for the sake of the Jakarta Post and also for the sake of the healthy Indonesian press," Mulya Lubis, a lawyer who represents the newspaper, told a news conference.
Lubis said negotiations for an out-of-court settlement were underway.
